title: The mystics in you
hookLine: mystics aren't a different species; they paid attention for a long time

cards: When people hear the word mystic, they often picture someone floating a few inches off the floor. Glowing eyes. Visions every Tuesday.
Someone simply built differently from the rest of us. But look at who you've actually met these twenty days. A soldier with a limp who cooked dinner.
A dyer's daughter. A sick woman in a small room. A monk who copied books.
A young man who couldn't find a minister to help him. A nun who didn't know how to begin her book. Not a different species.

teach.b: The word mystic comes from Greek. It shares a root with mystery, and goes back to a verb that means to close, the eyes or the lips. In the early church, mystical didn't mean spooky.

It meant hidden: the hidden meaning inside scripture, the hidden life of God in the bread and wine, the hidden depth inside an ordinary life. A mystic, in that old sense, has learned to see what's hidden in plain sight.
How did they learn? Look back. The abbas and ammas: give me a word, tend the fire, go to your cell and stay put.
Gregory: always further in. Benedict: pray and work, and treat the pots like altar vessels. Hildegard saw greening.
Bernard mapped four loves. Francis called the sun his brother. The Cloud: reached by love.
Julian, the anchoress, saw the hazelnut and heard a love bigger than the hurt. Catherine spoke up. The Imitation: follow quietly.
Teresa found a room further in; John found that dark is not absent. Brother Lawrence found God among the pots. Fox found that of God in everyone.
Under all of it runs one thread. They paid attention: to God, to scripture, to the people in front of them, to the ordinary thing in their hands. Not for a minute.
The Psalm puts it plainly: "Be still, and know that I am God." The mystics themselves said seeing God is a gift, not something anyone can earn or force.
But in their stories, again and again, the door opens where someone is looking.

how: Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant Christians read the mystics as companions in prayer, and some practice daily periods of quiet attention, such as silent prayer, slow scripture reading, or doing ordinary work with God in mind.

o: someone born with special powers to see visions
a fortune-teller who reads signs of the future
someone who learns to see God hidden in plain sight

games.q: which mystic said it — tap the pairs.

s: mystics are a special kind of person, born different
a cook, a dyer's daughter, a copyist monk: ordinary people who paid attention for years.
in the early church, mystical meant hidden
the hidden meaning in scripture and the hidden life of God in the sacraments.
Christians say you can force a vision of God with enough effort
seeing God is a gift; attention is where the door opens.

games.q: you've met twenty mystics in twenty days. what's the one thread that runs through all of them?
games.why: some had visions, others didn't; some were monks, others cooks and lay people. each of them paid attention.

practice: Choose one thing in front of you, your hand, a cup, the light on the wall, and look at it as if you'd never seen it before.

When the mind wanders, bring it back, like Brother Lawrence, without fuss; that small return, over and over, for years, is the thread these twenty days kept finding. If you pray, you can simply be still, and know.

wordCard.voice: Mystic. From a Greek word about closing the eyes: someone who learns to see what's hidden in plain sight.

orig.note: Greek: hidden, of the mysteries; from a verb meaning to close the eyes or lips.

carryVoice: Your line: attention is the beginning. That closes our stretch on the mystics. Tomorrow, the family of churches.

sources.q: Be still, and know that I am God
